title: Cyrus and the Letter
premise: In the winter of 1917, battlefield nurse Edmund Sterling keeps a secret ledger of soldiers whose names officers have struck from official records, believing that a person unrecorded was never truly lost. When a mute child is abandoned at her field hospital door with a note instructing her to forget his face, Edmund discovers the boy carries letters implicating a powerful family in wartime profiteering — and that the child's survival depends on reaching England aboard a ship with one berth left. As she navigates forged papers, a vengeful officer, and her own growing love for the boy, Edmund must decide whether to give the berth to the child, to a dying soldier from her ledger, or to herself. In the end, she surrenders her own passage, sends the boy to safety with the ledger as proof, and survives the war only to find him years later — grown, and carrying her name.
about_author: Emrys Sandoval is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing unsent letters from the First World War in provincial English collections. Their fiction is drawn from the marginalia, ration books, and hospital ledgers that history forgot to index.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Names
chapters.summary: Edmund Sterling, working a dressing station near Ypres, records in her private notebook the names of men erased from official rolls. POV: Edmund. Establishes her quiet rebellion and the emotional weight of remembrance; ends with the order to evacuate coming sooner than expected.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: As evacuation orders arrive, Edmund sorts her belongings into what fits in a kit bag, measuring her life in portable things. POV: Edmund. A meditation on loss and pragmatism; she burns letters she cannot carry, keeping only the ledger.

chapters.title: A Knock at the Door of the War
chapters.summary: During a bombardment, a five-year-old boy appears at the hospital entrance clutching a satchel, with a note: forget this face. POV: Edmund. Fear and tenderness collide as she takes him in against regulations.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Would Not Speak
chapters.summary: The child, whom Edmund names Cyrus for no reason she can explain, refuses to speak but clings to his satchel. POV: Edmund. She wins his trust through small kindnesses; the beat is fragile hope.

chapters.title: Satchel of Ash
chapters.summary: Edmund discovers the satchel holds sealed letters naming the Ashcombe family and their shipping contracts — evidence of profiteering and abandoned dependents. POV: Edmund. Dread replaces curiosity; she realizes the boy is not random debris of war but evidence.

chapters.title: Captain Vane's Inspection
chapters.summary: Captain Vane, an officer with polished manners and cold eyes, inspects the station and lingers over Cyrus. POV: Edmund. The menace is unspoken; Edmund lies smoothly for the first time and doesn't recognize herself after.

chapters.title: The Berth on the Calais Boat
chapters.summary: Word comes that a civilian evacuation ship will carry wounded and displaced to England — with limited places. POV: Edmund. Hope arrives with arithmetic: too many people, too few berths, and her name is not yet on any list.

chapters.title: Private Hollis, Dying Slowly
chapters.summary: Edmund tends Private Hollis, a shell-shocked soldier whose name appeared in her ledger after being struck off as a deserter. POV: Edmund. Guilt surfaces: she has recorded the forgotten but never fought for them.

chapters.title: Letters to No One
chapters.summary: Cyrus begins leaving folded paper offerings at Edmund's cot — drawings of a woman's face, burned at the edges. POV: Edmund. She realizes he watched someone die; grief becomes a language between them.

chapters.title: Vane Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Vane privately offers Edmund safe passage and protection if she hands over the satchel and the boy. POV: Edmund. Temptation wears a uniform; she stalls, and understands he will not ask twice.

chapters.title: The Matron's Bargain
chapters.summary: Matron Greer, exhausted and pragmatic, warns Edmund that harboring the child endangers every nurse in the station. POV: Edmund. Loyalty fractures along lines of survival; Edmund refuses to give Cyrus up, burning a bridge.

chapters.title: Night Train to the Coast
chapters.summary: The station receives sudden orders to move; Edmund smuggles Cyrus onto a hospital train among the wounded. POV: Edmund. Tension of near-discovery; a kind orderly, Tomas, covers for them at cost to himself.

chapters.title: What Tomas Knew
chapters.summary: Tomas reveals he once carried a similar satchel for another family and paid for it with his brother's life. POV: Edmund. The price of survival is named aloud; Edmund sees her possible future in him.

chapters.title: The Port at Boulogne
chapters.summary: They reach Boulogne to chaos: the ship delayed, refugees camped on the docks, Vane's adjutant asking questions. POV: Edmund. Claustrophobic dread; Edmund hides the ledger inside Cyrus's coat.

chapters.title: A Name on a List
chapters.summary: Edmund secures two provisional places — hers and Cyrus's — but learns Private Hollis has been transferred to the port, nameless and unfit to travel without a sponsor. POV: Edmund. The moral geometry tightens: three lives, shrinking room.

chapters.title: Hollis Remembers His Name
chapters.summary: Edmund tells Hollis she has kept his true name all these months; he weeps and asks her to make it mean something. POV: Edmund. The ledger transforms from record to promise; she cannot now let him vanish.

chapters.title: Vane Closes the Net
chapters.summary: Vane confronts Edmund on the dock, revealing he knows about the letters and offering again — this time with a threat against the nurses she left behind. POV: Edmund. Coercion dressed as courtesy; she agrees to think until dawn.

chapters.title: Cyrus Speaks
chapters.summary: In the night, Cyrus speaks his first words: not his own name, but the name of the dead woman in his drawings — his mother, the Ashcombes' housemaid. POV: Edmund. Devastating tenderness; the abstract evidence becomes a murdered girl.

chapters.title: The Arithmetic of Mercy
chapters.summary: Edmund counts berths, lies, debts: one place remains after the wounded board. Hollis, Cyrus, or herself. POV: Edmund. Cold clarity and hot grief; she drafts three versions of tomorrow and believes none of them.

chapters.title: Matron's Last Instruction
chapters.summary: A letter from Matron Greer reaches the port: hold the line, the family has friends everywhere, trust no officer. POV: Edmund. Solidarity across distance; Edmund stops feeling alone and starts feeling hunted together.

chapters.title: Boarding Call
chapters.summary: The ship's whistle sounds; wounded are carried up the gangway while Vane watches the crowd for a small boy. POV: Edmund. Rising panic choreographed against bureaucratic calm; the climax is now hours away.

chapters.title: The Forged Passage
chapters.summary: Edmund alters a travel chit using skills learned from the ledger — making the unrecorded legible. POV: Edmund. Her quiet art of names becomes open forgery; she feels the full weight of what survival costs.

chapters.title: Vane Finds the Satchel
chapters.summary: Vane's searchers seize Cyrus's coat with the hidden letters; the boy escapes into the dock crowds but the evidence is taken. POV: Edmund. Catastrophe; everything now depends on testimony, memory, and nerve.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Lamplight
chapters.summary: Vane questions Edmund in a customs office, dangling the fates of Greer and Tomas. POV: Edmund. A duel of composure; she gives him truth shaped like surrender, buying until morning.

chapters.title: Tomas Pays Again
chapters.summary: Tomas creates a diversion at the gate so Edmund can reach Cyrus, and is detained for it. POV: Edmund. Sacrifice compounds guilt; the price of survival is always paid by someone else first.

chapters.title: One Berth
chapters.summary: Final boarding: Edmund stands with Hollis and Cyrus before the gangway as the last call sounds. POV: Edmund. The choice made concrete; she lifts Cyrus toward the sailor's outstretched arms.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Forgot the Face
chapters.summary: Edmund puts the ledger in Cyrus's satchel, tells him to remember her face instead of forgetting it, and sends him up alone. POV: Edmund. Heartbreak as an act of faith; the ship pulls away carrying her whole reason.

chapters.title: Left on the Dock
chapters.summary: Edmund and Hollis watch the ship go as Vane approaches — but military police arrive first, summoned by Greer's allies in London. POV: Edmund. Reversal; Vane's confidence cracks as power shifts hands.

chapters.title: Arrest of Captain Vane
chapters.summary: Vane is taken for questioning over the Ashcombe contracts; the letters, copied by Greer before mailing, surface in Whitehall. POV: Edmund. Justice arrives imperfectly and late; vindication tastes like ash.

chapters.title: Winter of Waiting
chapters.summary: Edmund serves out the war in French hospitals, writing monthly letters to an address in Kent that never answer. POV: Edmund. Long ache of uncertainty; she measures days in patients saved and letters unanswered.

chapters.title: Armistice
chapters.summary: November 1918: bells, mud, strangers kissing in the street. Edmund reads the casualty lists looking for names from her ledger. POV: Edmund. Grief and relief indistinguishable; she goes home to a country that forgot how to say thank you.

chapters.title: The House in Kent
chapters.summary: Demobilized, Edmund travels to the address on her letters and finds an empty cottage and a neighbor who remembers 'the little gentleman who left.' POV: Edmund. Hope deferred; the trail is cold but not dead.

chapters.title: Ledger of the Living
chapters.summary: Edmund takes work in a London records office, quietly restoring struck-off names to official memory, including Hollis's. POV: Edmund. Purpose rebuilt from wreckage; belonging found in service rather than blood.

chapters.title: A Letter, Finally
chapters.summary: Seven years on, a letter arrives in careful childish-then-grown handwriting: Cyrus, raised by a Quaker family, kept the ledger and her face in memory. POV: Edmund. Joy arriving like weather after drought; she reads it standing in the rain.

chapters.title: The Meeting at Charing Cross
chapters.summary: Edmund waits at the station clock, terrified the boy will not recognize the woman who forgot nothing. POV: Edmund. Suspended breath; then a young man says her name — the one she gave him — and the years collapse.

chapters.title: What Was Inherited
chapters.summary: Cyrus shows Edmund the ledger, annotated over years with names of others he has found and restored. POV: Edmund. The theme lands: inheritance is not property but practice; her rebellion became his vocation.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Cyrus, now studying law, prepares to testify in the reopened Ashcombe inquiry; Edmund gives her account of the mother's letters. POV: Edmund. Closure without erasure; the dead maid finally gets her name spoken in a courtroom.

chapters.title: The Last Entry
chapters.summary: Edmund writes the final entry in the original ledger: not a death, but a homecoming. POV: Edmund. Quiet triumph; the book of the forgotten closes on a remembered man.

chapters.title: Belonging
chapters.summary: Years later, Edmund and Cyrus share a modest Christmas dinner with Hollis, Greer, and Tomas's sister; Cyrus calls her family without ceremony. POV: Edmund. Resolution in warmth and ordinariness; belonging chosen, not granted.

chapters.title: Coda: The Face Worth Remembering
chapters.summary: Edmund, old, visits the sea wall at Boulogne where the ship once pulled away, and finds a plaque Cyrus commissioned bearing both their names. POV: Edmund. Final beat: what can be carried when the orders come is each other.
